scope: First 11 user-supplied program websites, inspected for research agendas and concrete projects, not application deadlines or endorsement of a thesis idea.
method: Official program/project pages opened. Access status distinguishes page availability from whether specific project details could be verified. No inference of fit from program name alone.

programs.name: Apart Research
programs.access_status: Accessible; fellowship and research pages read.
programs.agenda: Technical AI-safety projects spanning evaluations, interpretability, multi-agent systems, and technical governance; fellows can develop their own ideas or partner agendas.

projects.title: Noise Injection Reveals Hidden Capabilities of Sandbagging Language Models
projects.status: NeurIPS 2025 conference PDF; title/abstract inspected, not full paper.
projects.relevance: Shows that numerical perturbation response as a behavioral diagnostic is not itself a new research principle. No attack reproduction was performed.

programs.fit_assessment: Potential fit for a sharply measured numerical reliability project; fellowship breadth is not evidence that a generic safety wrapper is novel.

programs.name: Pivotal Research
programs.access_status: Non-www initial open failed; www page returned mostly navigation. The specific Q3 roster was not verified. Official library projects were accessible.
programs.agenda: Verified library includes technical governance and post-deployment evaluation integrity; do not treat accessible library projects as the Q3 2026 roster.

projects.title: Silent Updates: Measuring and Closing the Post-Deployment Disclosure Gap
projects.relevance: Studies changes to fine-tuning, classifiers, prompts, retrieval, and routing after evaluation, with disclosure/behavior triggers. Closest program-level connection to ensuring that deployed behavior still matches the evaluated artifact; not a hardware fault-recovery mechanism.

projects.title: Privacy-Preserving AI Verification
projects.status: Official page opened; not relied on for technical mechanism.
projects.relevance: Adjacent verification agenda only; no mechanism claim inferred.

programs.fit_assessment: Relevant to evaluation-to-deployment contracts if a precise technical boundary is defined.

programs.name: ERA Fellowship
programs.access_status: Program, AI-risks, and research-project listing pages accessible and read.
programs.agenda: Technical safety: robustness/control, objectives and misalignment, interpretability. Technical governance: hardware-use monitoring, evaluations/standards, compute governance, structured access, safety cases.

projects.title: Verifiable Semiconductor Manufacturing
projects.status: Official Oxford AIGI publication page read; April 2026.
projects.relevance: Fabrication-chain threat model and tiered assurance make hardware trust a measurable governance problem; not silent-data-corruption recovery.

projects.title: Towards Reliable Evaluation of Behavior Steering Interventions in LLMs
projects.status: Title verified on official listing; linked PDF fetch failed.
projects.relevance: Evaluation reliability is adjacent, but full mechanism was not verified.

programs.fit_assessment: Strong explicit bridge between hardware assurance and technical safety, but system guarantees must connect to a concrete risk.

programs.name: LASR Labs
programs.access_status: Non-www initial open failed; www homepage and past-project pages accessible.
programs.agenda: Technical AI-safety research grounded in concrete loss-of-control threat models; past work includes probe generalization, fine-tuning fragility, interpretability, and evaluation awareness.

projects.title: The Impact of Off-Policy Training Data on Probe Generalisation
projects.status: Primary arXiv abstract page opened; preprint.
projects.relevance: Probe portability across distributions is already an explicit research target; any runtime-transformation monitor project must distinguish itself.

projects.title: A loss curvature account of fine-tuning fragility
projects.status: Official listing states ICML 2026 workshops; linked paper fetch failed. Not represented as main-conference acceptance.
projects.relevance: Mechanistic numerical accounts of behavioral fragility are adjacent.

programs.fit_assessment: Fit requires a causal threat-model argument; ordinary latency improvement alone is insufficient.

programs.name: AI Safety Camp
programs.access_status: Accessible redirect to current Google-Sites-backed Research Incubator page; project catalog not established from inspected page.
programs.agenda: Research incubation from conceptual confusion to testable research directions; no specific hardware project verified.
programs.fit_assessment: Useful research-development format, not evidence for a particular systems thesis or its novelty.

programs.name: Principles of Intelligence / PIBBSS
programs.access_status: Fellowship and PIRAMID project pages accessible and read.
programs.agenda: Foundational alignment-oriented inquiry; tracks include AIXI, gradual disempowerment, safe Pareto improvements, and corrigibility.

projects.title: PIRAMID
projects.relevance: Theory-informed interpretability connects formal/toy models to real behaviors, synthetic data, and rare/worst-case prediction. Supports a formal-model-plus-falsification method, not a direct KV-recovery endorsement.

programs.fit_assessment: A mechanistic theory of error propagation with testable predictions would be a closer fit than an engineering wrapper.

programs.name: Anthropic Fellows Program
programs.access_status: Official program page accessible and read.
programs.agenda: Oversight, robustness/control, model organisms, interpretability, security, and model welfare.

projects.title: Open-sourcing circuit-tracing tools
projects.relevance: Fellow-led tooling constructs attribution graphs for open-weight models and tests hypotheses through interventions. Relevant standard: identify and test a causal mechanism, not simply correlate output quality with perturbations.

programs.fit_assessment: Numerical systems work needs a credible connection to safety-relevant causal behavior. Program presence does not prove a project is novel or supported.

programs.name: OpenAI Safety Fellowship
programs.access_status: Official announcement accessible and read; OpenAI Docs skill consulted before official-source lookup.
programs.agenda: Pilot announcement lists safety evaluations, ethics, robustness, scalable mitigations, privacy-preserving safety, and agent oversight.
programs.fit_assessment: Broad robustness/evaluation fit; no concrete project roster or hardware-specific agenda verified. Do not infer acceptance likelihood or institutional endorsement.

programs.name: Iliad Fellowship
programs.access_status: Non-www initial open failed; www official fellowship page accessible and read.
programs.agenda: Three-month applied-mathematics alignment research fellowship with mentored independent work.
programs.fit_assessment: A theory-led reliability contract might fit the method; no specific hardware/KV project catalog verified.

programs.name: GovAI
programs.access_status: Non-www initial open failed; www opportunities and concrete research page accessible.
programs.agenda: AI governance, including technical governance and risk management.

projects.title: Open Problems in Technical AI Governance
projects.status: Official research overview read; July 2024. Full linked paper not read.
projects.relevance: Technical tools can support assessment, enforcement, incentives, and compliance. A runtime reliability contract needs a clear decision or assurance claim it enables.

programs.fit_assessment: Governance relevance is a separate argument from hardware-system novelty; do not relabel a systems optimization as governance without a user and decision.

programs.name: IAPS Fellowship
programs.access_status: Non-www initial open failed; www fellowship, research listing, and concrete research page accessible.
programs.agenda: Policy-oriented AI-risk research; the inspected research includes preserving oversight under efficiency pressures.

projects.title: Policy Options for Preserving Chain of Thought Monitorability
projects.status: Official research page opened and official listing read.
projects.relevance: Efficiency pressures can remove readable chain-of-thought, threatening oversight. This motivates studying observability loss, but is policy work rather than evidence for a novel cache-repair mechanism.

programs.fit_assessment: Potential impact argument about preserving monitorability; weak direct fit for a hardware performance thesis absent a policy-relevant measurement.
